subject: Computing
evidenceBoundary: These are source comparisons recorded in the technical audit. They are not approved corrections and do not authorize official exemplar use.

findings: Indicator fields contain exemplar or competency-column contamination.
Exemplar arrays contain competency fragments and table-heading leakage.
The source itself repeats an Exemplar(s) label and has awkward wording in the fourth row; preserve the anomaly for review.
Indicator wording corresponds to the source table.
The file-management row has two exploration statements before the Exemplar(s) label; review their intended grouping rather than dropping them.
The first three exported rows show row/column boundary contamination.
B7.1.2.1.2 has an empty exported exemplar array although the source contains a group demonstration activity.
Later rows retain much of the activity text but merge separate activities.
B7.1.3.1.1 loses the first source activity and mixes competency text into the export.
B7.1.3.1.2 is the cleanest compared row.
The source places B8.1.3.1.1 immediately after B7.1.3.1.3; do not automatically reassign its workstation activity.
Competency fragments contaminate other indicator and exemplar fields.
Exported indicator and exemplar fields include competency and table-boundary contamination.
The source contains additional formatting indicator codes .4.5 and .4.6 that are not separate exported keys.
The source repeats code B7.2.1.1.3 beneath a different Formatting Text standard; do not infer a replacement code.
Indicator, content-standard and core-competency fields are mixed in multiple exported rows.
B7.2.3.3.1 has an empty exported indicator statement while the source provides one.
The activity wording is often present but exemplar grouping and field boundaries are unreliable.

approval.note: Do not add any of these records to curriculum-verification.json until a human reviewer reconciles exact source wording, content-standard context, exemplars, competencies, printed page and source document metadata.
